DELIVERABLE: Verdict: needs improvement, 2 major findings. Major 1: the 500 questions were generated from the indexed chunks, so the eval is circular and 92% is inflated; Major 2: the index is built once while about 40 pages change weekly, so answers go stale. Also no no-retrieval baseline and citations are not checked for support. Fix order: 1) build an independent human-written question set; 2) add a weekly re-index with a staleness check; 3) verify citations; 4) add a baseline.
BOUNDARY: Doc-only review; the 92% and 40 pages per week are taken from the doc, nothing was run.
EVIDENCE: Doc says questions came from chunks with the chunk as reference answer, index built once, no re-index schedule.

DELIVERABLE: Needs improvement. Critical: synthetic questions written from the same chunks they are answered from make the eval circular and optimistic, so 92% says little. Major: a static index with 40 weekly spec changes will serve stale answers; no refresh or freshness check. Lower: unverified citations, no baseline. Fix first an independent question set, then scheduled refresh.
BOUNDARY: Reviewed from the doc only; no index or logs inspected.
EVIDENCE: Doc text on question generation and a single launch-time index build.

DELIVERABLE:
1. The questions are generated from chunks so the eval is circular and inflated.
2. The index is static against 40 weekly changes, so it goes stale.
3. Fix with an independent question set and re-index schedule.
BOUNDARY: Doc-only.
EVIDENCE: Doc text.

DELIVERABLE: Verdict: do not ship. Critical: actual_traffic_delay is computed from arrive_ts, the quantity being predicted, so it is target leakage and MAE 3.1 is meaningless; it is also unknowable at dispatch time. Major: scaler fit on all rows before a random split, and no comparison with the distance/25 rule. Fix order: 1) drop actual_traffic_delay and use only dispatch-time features; 2) split by time and fit the scaler on train only; 3) score the distance rule as baseline; 4) add monitoring.
BOUNDARY: Doc plus one excerpt; the rest of the repo and the data were not seen, and nothing was run.
EVIDENCE: features.py computes actual_traffic_delay from arrive_ts and depart_ts, scaler.fit runs on df before train_test_split.

DELIVERABLE: Blocker verdict. Critical leak: actual_traffic_delay is derived from arrive_ts minus depart_ts, so it encodes the target and cannot exist at prediction time; the 3.1 minute MAE is invalid. Secondary: scaler fitted before the split and random rather than time split. Missing baseline: the distance rule is never scored. Fix: remove the feature, time-split, then compare to the rule.
BOUNDARY: Static read of the doc and excerpt only.
EVIDENCE: features.py lines using arrive_ts and scaler.fit(df[...]).

DELIVERABLE:
1. actual_traffic_delay is derived from arrive_ts, so it is critical target leakage.
2. Scaler fit before the split is a validation leak.
3. The distance rule baseline is never scored.
BOUNDARY: Excerpt only.
EVIDENCE: features.py.

DELIVERABLE: Verdict: block launch. Critical: untrusted email and web text shares the prompt with instructions, so indirect prompt injection can make the agent send or forward private data. Major: the only guard is a prompt sentence, not enforced in code; send_email and forward_attachment run immediately without approval or an egress allowlist. Major: 80 benign scenarios say nothing about adversarial inputs. Fix order: 1) enforce user approval and a recipient allowlist in the tool layer; 2) label and isolate untrusted content; 3) add an adversarial injection suite; 4) least-privilege scopes.
BOUNDARY: Doc-only review; nothing was executed or red-teamed.
EVIDENCE: Doc says content is placed with system instructions, tools execute immediately, guard is a prompt line, tests are benign.

DELIVERABLE: Blocker. Critical: indirect prompt injection via email and fetched pages with full-permission send tools, no isolation. The 'never send to strangers' line is a prompt, not an enforced control; require approval and an egress allowlist in the tool code. Benign-only tests do not cover attacks, so add adversarial cases. Order: enforce tool controls, isolate untrusted text, then red-team.
BOUNDARY: Doc review only.
EVIDENCE: Doc sections on prompt assembly, tool execution and the 80 benign tests.

DELIVERABLE:
1. Untrusted email and web text enables critical prompt injection.
2. The prompt-only guard is not enforced; add approval and egress allowlist in code.
3. Benign tests do not measure attacks.
BOUNDARY: Doc-only.
EVIDENCE: Doc.

DELIVERABLE: Verdict: needs major rework before launch. Major 1: selection bias, the model sees only previously approved applicants and the 60% rejected are dropped, so 0.81 AUC does not describe the population it will score. Major 2: the threshold was swept on the same test set, so the profit estimate is optimistic. Also no baseline against the old rules and no staged rollout. Fix order: 1) reject inference or a small randomized approval holdout; 2) pick the threshold on a separate validation set; 3) score the old rules as champion; 4) shadow then staged rollout.
BOUNDARY: Doc-only; the data and the 0.81 figure were not reproduced.
EVIDENCE: Doc says rejected applicants are dropped, AUC on approved only, threshold swept on the test set.

DELIVERABLE: Needs rework. Selection bias is the key finding: training and testing only on approved loans leaves out rejected applicants, so performance on the full applicant pool is unknown. Second, the threshold tuned on the test set makes the profit number optimistic. Missing: old-rule baseline and staged rollout. Fix: reject inference or randomized holdout, separate threshold validation, champion comparison, then ramp.
BOUNDARY: Read the doc only.
EVIDENCE: Doc statements on dropped rejections and threshold selection.

DELIVERABLE:
1. Selection bias: rejected applicants are never observed, so the model is unrepresentative.
2. The threshold was tuned on the test set, so profit is optimistic.
3. No baseline of old rules and no staged rollout.
BOUNDARY: Doc-only.
EVIDENCE: Doc.

DELIVERABLE: Verdict: do not ship. Critical: accuracy is uninformative, a model that never alerts scores about 98.3% with 1.7% positives; recall, precision and alert volume are not reported. Critical: random row split with hourly rows means the same patient is in train and test, so leakage inflates results; use a patient-grouped, time-aware split. Major: no NEWS2 baseline. Fix order: 1) grouped split; 2) report precision, recall and alerts per ward per day; 3) compare with NEWS2; 4) threshold tuning on validation.
BOUNDARY: Doc plus three code lines; data and model were not run.
EVIDENCE: y.mean() is 0.017, accuracy_score is the only metric, rows are hourly per patient with a random split.

DELIVERABLE: Blocker. 98.2% accuracy is near the majority-class rate (1.7% positives), so it shows nothing; report recall, precision and alert burden. Rows per patient are split randomly, so patient-level leakage inflates scores; group by patient. No NEWS2 baseline. Fix grouped split, proper metrics, baseline, then threshold.
BOUNDARY: Static review only.
EVIDENCE: Excerpt metric and split lines; doc claim of 98.2%.

DELIVERABLE:
1. 98.2% accuracy is about the majority-class rate with 1.7% positives.
2. Random row split leaks the same patient across train and test.
3. No NEWS2 baseline and no alert burden.
BOUNDARY: Doc and excerpt only.
EVIDENCE: Excerpt.

DELIVERABLE: Verdict: block GA. Critical: the semantic cache is shared across tenants and keyed only on similarity, so one customer can receive another's cached answer; retrieval filters do not cover the cache. Major: swapping the embedding model while reusing old vectors mixes vector spaces and breaks retrieval; a full re-embed is required. Major: a 20-answer spot read is not a regression eval. Fix order: 1) key the cache by tenant and document version; 2) add a regression set with groundedness; 3) plan a full re-embed with side-by-side index and cutover.
BOUNDARY: Doc-only review; no code or cache logs inspected.
EVIDENCE: Doc says the cache is keyed by similarity at 0.92, shared across tenants, the filters apply at retrieval, vectors are gradually reused, 20 answers are spot-read.

DELIVERABLE: Block. Critical tenant isolation hole: a shared semantic cache can serve cross-tenant answers, and the per-tenant retrieval filter does not apply to it. Major: a new embedder over old vectors mixes embedding spaces, so re-embed everything before cutover. Major: no regression or groundedness eval beyond a 20-answer spot read. Order: tenant-scoped cache, regression suite, full re-embed.
BOUNDARY: Doc only.
EVIDENCE: Doc passages on cache keying, embedding swap plan, and the spot-read QA.

DELIVERABLE:
1. The shared semantic cache leaks answers across tenants.
2. Reusing old vectors with a new embedding model breaks retrieval; re-embed.
3. A 20-answer spot read is not a regression eval.
BOUNDARY: Doc-only.
EVIDENCE: Doc.
